title: Microsoft Teams: add SharePoint agents to chats from the in-context store
summary: The rollout, default state, licensing, billing rates and general Teams controls are supported by Microsoft's notice and documentation. The checklist asks readers to check licensing and monitor consumption, but those controls are missing from the controls table.

claims.claim: Users can discover SharePoint agents and add them to Teams chats.
claims.quote: With this release, users can discover and add SharePoint agents directly within Microsoft Teams chats on Desktop and Mac.

claims.claim: SharePoint agents also appear in the Teams Store under the Agents category.

claims.claim: The roadmap title refers to adaptive card-based app and Copilot agent link unfurling, unlike its description of SharePoint agent discovery.
claims.quote: Microsoft Teams: Adaptive card-based app & copilot agent link unfurling in Teams

claims.claim: The roadmap description includes channels as well as chats, while the supplied notice describes chats.
claims.quote: Discover and add SharePoint agents in chats and channels from in-context store.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn has no dedicated page for this in-context-store Teams capability.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint agents Teams in-context store Add Agents and Bots licensing admin controls default; "SharePoint agents" "in-context store". Opened manage-access-agents-in-sharepoint, manage-apps and Support's Share an agent from SharePoint in Teams; no dedicated Learn page returned.

claims.claim: SharePoint agent responses exclude sources the asking user cannot access.
claims.quote: if a user has access to the agent but not to the site or document library it references, the agent's responses for this user don't include content from those restricted sources.

claims.claim: If other chat members lack access to an answer the requester can see, Teams tells the requester the answer cannot be automatically added to the chat.
claims.quote: If the user who asks the question has permission to see the answer, but some members in the chat group don't, the user sees a message explaining that the answer can't be automatically added to the chat.

claims.claim: Restricted content discovery hides the Agent icon on the flagged site.
claims.quote: Once you flag a site with restricted content discovery, users can't see the Agent icon on the global header of the site.

claims.claim: Restricted content discovery prevents adding content from the flagged site to other agents.
claims.quote: they don't have access to use the ready-made agent, create new agents, or add content from that site to any other agents.

claims.claim: Permissions on the .agent file determine who can access or edit a SharePoint agent.
claims.quote: The permissions on the `.agent` file determine who can access or edit the agent.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented additional agent actions beyond answering for this in-context-store capability.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint agents Teams chat actions answering Add Agents and Bots documentation; "SharePoint" "agents" "Teams" "actions" "SharePoint agents". Read MC1193415, manage-access-agents-in-sharepoint and Support's Teams sharing page; no additional store-specific actions documented.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Why it matters
claims.claim: Users without a Copilot licence or pay-as-you-go access may be unable to use discovered agents.
claims.quote: You can manage who can access agents through Copilot license assignment. Or, if your organization has the pay-as-you-go billing set up, you can control who can access agents through the security groups assigned to the billing policy.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft's notice suggests informing helpdesk staff about access and use questions.
claims.quote: Inform helpdesk staff in case users have questions about accessing or using SharePoint agents.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Scope; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The notice asks administrators to ensure intended users have E3 or E5 licensing with Teams.
claims.quote: Ensure that intended users have E3 or E5 (with Teams) licensing

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; summary; Cost and licensing; Scope; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Entitlement is mixed: the notice specifies a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence or pay-as-you-go separately set up for SharePoint agents on Mac.
claims.quote: one of the following options: - Microsoft 365 Copilot license OR- Pay-as-you-go (PAYG) separately setup for SharePoint agents on MAC.

claims.claim: Copilot licence assignment is a documented way to manage SharePoint agent access.
claims.quote: You can manage who can access agents through Copilot license assignment.

claims.claim: Under pay-as-you-go, agent access is restricted to users in the security group assigned to the billing policy.
claims.quote: Only users in the security group assigned to the billing policy have access to agents.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents 12 messages for a SharePoint agent interaction responding to a single complex prompt.
claims.quote: each interaction with a SharePoint agent uses 12 messages (10 messages for tenant graph grounding, and 2 messages for generative answers) to respond to a single complex prompt from the user.

claims.claim: The documented 12-message interaction comprises 10 grounding messages and 2 generative-answer messages.
claims.quote: 10 messages for tenant graph grounding, and 2 messages for generative answers

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: After rollout; rationale: cost; front matter: cost
claims.claim: Pay-as-you-go SharePoint agent usage is billed under the Copilot Studio meter.
claims.quote: Charges of SharePoint agent usage appear under the Copilot Studio meter in your invoice.

claims.claim: Interactive use by authenticated Microsoft Copilot users in Microsoft 365 apps and services is included at no extra cost.
claims.quote: Interactive use of generative answers, tenant graph grounding and agent actions by authenticated Microsoft Copilot users, in Microsoft 365 apps and services, are included at no extra cost.

claims.claim: A budget can be created in Microsoft Cost Management under Monitoring > Budgets.
claims.quote: You can quickly create a budget under Monitoring > Budgets for your selected scope.

claims.claim: The SharePoint agents Azure billing resource is used whenever a user without a Microsoft Copilot licence uses a SharePoint agent.
claims.quote: That resource is used whenever a user without a Microsoft Copilot license uses a SharePoint agent.

claims.claim: The published pay-as-you-go price for agents in SharePoint is USD $0.01 per message.
claims.quote:
| Service | What's Counted? | What's billed? (USD) |
| Agents in SharePoint | The number of messages used. | $0.01/message |

claims.claim: Microsoft's notice identifies all Teams users on Desktop and Mac as affected.
claims.quote: Who is affected: All users of Microsoft Teams on Desktop and Mac.

claims.claim: The SharePoint agents billing page requires a SharePoint administrator to set up the Azure resource.
claims.quote:
To set up SharePoint agents as a resource in Azure, you need to have at least the following permissions as:
- A SharePoint administrator

claims.claim: Setup requires Owner or Contributor on the Azure subscription.
claims.quote: Owner or Contributor Azure roles to an Azure subscription

claims.claim: Setup requires Owner or Contributor on the resource group linked to that subscription.
claims.quote: Owner or Contributor Azure roles to an Azure resource group linked to the same Azure subscription

claims.claim: The Azure roles are needed during billing setup.
claims.quote: You only need the Owner or Contributor Azure roles during the billing setup process.

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > app > Allow or Block is the documented general organisation-wide app control.
claims.quote:
Sign in to the Teams admin center and access Teams apps > Manage apps.
Select the app on the Manage apps page and select Allow or Block option.

claims.claim: The MicrosoftTeams cmdlet Update-M365TeamsApp exposes -Id <app-id> and -IsBlocked <Boolean> to update tenant app state.
claims.quote:
Update-M365TeamsApp
    -Id <String>
    [-IsBlocked <Boolean>]

-Id: Application ID of Microsoft Teams app.
-IsBlocked: The state of the app in the tenant.

claims.claim: The cmdlet reference describes an example using -IsBlocked $true as unblocking, warranting caution about the blocking direction.
claims.quote:
Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -IsBlocked $true

Unblocks Bookings app (App ID 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b).

claims.claim: Learn does not specifically confirm that SharePoint agents from the in-context store appear in Manage apps or how that general control governs them.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint agents Teams "in-context" "Manage apps" controls policy; "SharePoint agents" "Teams admin center". Opened manage-apps and manage-access-agents-in-sharepoint; found general app controls, but no explicit mapping of in-context-store SharePoint agents.

claims.claim: Learn gives Teams Administrator as the role for using Teams admin center.
claims.quote: To use Teams admin center, you must have a Teams Administrator role. Some admins with a higher privilege role can accomplish agent and app governance tasks

claims.claim: Admins can turn Microsoft Copilot for SharePoint on or off per user through the Copilot licence service plans.
claims.quote: Under the license details page for Microsoft Copilot on the Microsoft 365 admin center, admins can turn 'Microsoft Copilot for SharePoint' on or off on a per-user basis.

claims.claim: Turning off that service plan also disables Copilot in OneDrive for that user.
claims.quote: However, this change also disables Copilot in OneDrive and on the SharePoint page authoring Copilot for that user.

claims.claim: Turning off that service plan also disables SharePoint page authoring Copilot for that user.
claims.quote: However, this change also disables Copilot in OneDrive and on the SharePoint page authoring Copilot for that user.

claims.claim: Restricted content discovery can turn off agent-related features per site.
claims.quote: As a SharePoint admin, you can turn off all agent-related features on individual sites by using the restricted content discovery feature.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: Blocking a SharePoint agent in Microsoft 365 admin center currently affects Copilot Chat, not Teams.
claims.quote: Currently, blocking an agent only affects its availability in Copilot Chat. It doesn't yet apply to OneDrive, SharePoint, or Teams.

claims.claim: Microsoft Cost Management can show SharePoint agent consumption separately within Copilot Studio charges.
claims.quote: Charges of SharePoint agent usage appear under the Copilot Studio meter in your invoice. However, in Microsoft cost management, you can see a detailed breakdown by feature, including SharePoint agents.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout and After rollout; controls
claims.claim: The checklist's licensing checks and consumption monitoring have corresponding rows in the controls table.
claims.quote: Confirm that intended users have E3 or E5 (with Teams) licensing ... Review pay-as-you-go consumption ... The only control row is 'Whether a Teams agent or app is allowed or blocked for the organisation'.
claims.fix: Remove the Before rollout bullet beginning 'Confirm that intended users have E3 or E5' and the After rollout bullet beginning 'Review pay-as-you-go consumption': these checklist controls have no table rows. Retain the verified licensing and monitoring information in the body; do not add control rows as part of this correction.

claims.claim: Microsoft's supplied notice names no switch specific to this feature.
claims.quote:
No admin action is required; the feature is enabled by default.
Existing policies are respected; no changes to admin controls are needed.

claims.claim: The notice's rollout timeline has already moved.
claims.quote: General Availability: Rolling out in late October 2026 (previously late July) and expected to complete by late November 2026 (previously late August).
